text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak to recieve message from Assad and to discuss developements in the peace process with Syria's Vice President Khaddam and Foreign Minister Shara.

- Foreign Minister Moussa says, ahead of talks between Mubarak and King Juan Carlos, that Egypt places great importance on the king's visit and that relations between Egypt and Spain are strong in all fields.
- Zamalek win the African Super Cup for the second time.
- Al-Azhar Grand Sheikh condemns the attack on the church at Abu Qurqas. The Sheikh and the religious affairs minister will head a religious delegation to offer condolences.
- Economy minister says Egyptian banks to take part in 42 projects worth six billion pounds.
- EgyptAir to offer between 10 to 20 percent of its capital as bonds. Each bond is worth $20,000 and individuals are allowed a maximum of five bonds.
- Public Enterprise minister says government's plan to privatise 73 companies this year will create 700,000 jobs.

- The war of deception against national banks. Akhbar warns of the danger of wicked advertisments aimed at traditional banks. Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar says traditional banks are closer to Islamic priniciples.
- Finance minister says new budget will rise to 82 billion pounds from 77.5 billion pounds.
- Building to start soon on gas export station in Arish. Station will be used to export gas to Turkey, Israel, Lebanon, Jordan and Palestine and will cost 4 billion pounds.
- Grand Mufti says women can hold leadership posts except presidency.
- Interior Ministry says it has determined identity of four gunmen responsible for Abu Qurqas attack.
- Prime minister to head meeting today to value land tht will be used in large industrial, tourism and agricultural projects.
- Parliament head says while attending conference in India that partnership between men and women boosts democracy, development and human rights.
